title: Best Badminton Shoes in India (2026)
summary: Three Kuikma badminton shoes from Decathlon India for first-timers and regular players, with the sole type from each shop page.
description: Helps Indian badminton players pick a first or next pair: three Kuikma shoes with non-marking soles, who each suits and what to check.
lead: Which badminton shoes can you buy in India right now, and which ones list a non-marking sole? This guide covers three Kuikma shoes from Decathlon India. One is for first-timers, one is for regular players and one is for players who want more cushioning. We picked them because each Decathlon India page states the sole type and showed the shoe as in stock when we read it. None was hand-tested. Everything here comes from shop pages, and we mark what is the maker's claim.

picks.name: Kuikma BS 190 (Decathlon India)
picks.label: For first-timers
picks.verdict: A simple lace-up court shoe for people new to badminton who play now and then. The page states a non-marking sole.
paragraphs: The Kuikma BS 190 is Decathlon's own-brand shoe for beginners. The Decathlon India page says it is for someone starting to discover badminton on court. The spec list shows a non-marking outsole, a low shoe with laces and a leather and mesh upper (the leather is synthetic). It also lists indoor parquet flooring and occasional play. The Budget tier is our own rough judgement about who it suits, not about cost.

Decathlon says the sole has a hummingbird-pattern rubber texture for grip. It says the midsole is EVA for cushioning and the mesh and PU upper is breathable. These are the maker's words, not independent findings. The page shows about 4.5 out of 5 from 319 ratings, a 2-year warranty and 30 days return. The shoe showed as in stock. Sizes load on the page, so check your own size. The page lists no shoe weight.
good: The Decathlon India page states a non-marking outsole and indoor parquet use
Aimed at beginners who play occasionally (per Decathlon)
Shows about 4.5 out of 5 from 319 ratings, with a 2-year warranty and 30 days return
not_good: No shoe weight is given on the page
The insole is listed as not removable, which matters if you use your own insole
Made for occasional play, so a regular player may want more cushioning and support

picks.name: Kuikma BS 530 (Decathlon India)
picks.label: For regular players
cells: Yes, gum sole per Decathlon India
picks.verdict: A cushioned, breathable shoe for people who play a few times a week. It is the only one of the three with a weight and court type written on the page.
paragraphs: The Kuikma BS 530 is for an intermediate player who wants good cushioning and a light, breathable upper, says Decathlon. The page answers common questions directly. It says the pair weighs about 560 g and can be used on wooden and synthetic courts. It says the shoe is non-marking with a gum sole and suits play 2 to 3 times a week. The Mid-range tier is our own judgement.

Decathlon says the two-piece sole and the PU foam and EVA insock add cushioning. It says the seamless upper helps with breathability. These are the maker's claims. The page shows about 4.4 out of 5 from 430 ratings, a 2-year warranty and 30 days return. The shoe showed as in stock. Decathlon advises hand washing and air drying only. It also says a non-marking shoe worn outdoors should not go back on an indoor court, because it can leave marks.
good: The page gives a weight (about 560 g for the pair) and says it suits wooden and synthetic courts
The page says it is a non-marking shoe with a gum sole
Made for regular play of 2 to 3 times a week (per Decathlon)
Shows about 4.4 out of 5 from 430 ratings and a 2-year warranty
not_good: The insole is listed as not removable
Decathlon does not recommend wearing it outdoors if you want to keep using it indoors
Care is hand washing and air drying only

picks.name: Kuikma BS Perform 590 (Decathlon India)
picks.label: For players who want more cushioning
picks.verdict: The most feature-rich of the three, with heel and forefoot cushioning and a twist-control part. It has far fewer buyer ratings.
paragraphs: The BS Perform 590 is for an intermediate player who wants strong cushioning and a bouncy take-off, says Decathlon. The page lists a non-marking outsole, a mesh and microfibre upper, a removable insole, laces and indoor use. Play frequency is listed as regular. We placed it in the Premium tier by our own judgement because it has the most features of the three, not because of cost.

Decathlon names a DHN cushion system under the heel and the front of the foot. It also names an InUp insert for take-off and a TPU anti-twist part for stability. These are the maker's claims. The page shows 4.9 out of 5, but from only 31 ratings, so treat that score with care. It shows a 2-year warranty and 30 days replacement, which is different wording from the other two. The shoe showed as in stock. Sizes are given in UK and EU. The page lists no shoe weight.
good: The page states a non-marking outsole
Has a removable insole, while the BS 190 and BS 530 pages list the insole as not removable
Decathlon names cushioning under the heel and front foot, plus a twist-control part (the maker's claim)
Sizes are shown in both UK and EU
not_good: Only 31 ratings, so the high score is less reliable
No shoe weight on the page
Return wording is '30 days replacement', so read the policy before ordering

choose.heading: Look for a non-marking sole
choose.text: Many indoor courts expect shoes that do not leave marks. This is general advice, so ask your court. All three shoes here show 'non marking' in the Decathlon India spec list. The BS 530 page adds that such shoes should not be used outdoors, as they can then leave marks indoors.

choose.heading: Match the shoe to how often you play
choose.text: Decathlon lists the BS 190 for occasional play. It lists the BS 530 and BS Perform 590 for regular play. The BS 530 page says 2 to 3 times a week. If you play now and then, a basic shoe is usually enough.

choose.heading: Do not use running shoes
choose.text: This is general advice. Badminton shoes are made for side steps and quick stops and starts. Running shoes are built for moving forward.

choose.heading: Check the size and size chart
choose.text: Sizes on these pages are UK sizes. The BS Perform 590 page also shows EU sizes. Stock by size loads on the page, so check yours before you order. Sizing can differ between brands, so read the size guide or try the shoe in a store.

choose.heading: Weight is a trade-off
choose.text: Lighter shoes suit fast footwork. Heavier ones often add cushioning. Of these three, only the BS 530 page gives a weight, about 560 g for the pair. The other pages do not list one, so you cannot compare them on weight.

choose.heading: Read warranty, returns and stock on the exact listing
choose.text: All three pages show a 2-year warranty. The BS 190 and BS 530 show 30 days return. The BS Perform 590 shows 30 days replacement. Colour pages are separate listings, so check the one you want. Also check that the shoe is in stock in your size.

faq.q: Can I play badminton in running shoes?
faq.a: It is better not to. This is general advice. Running shoes are made for forward movement. Badminton shoes are made for side steps and quick stops.

faq.q: What is a non-marking sole and why does it matter?
faq.a: It is a sole that does not leave dark marks on the floor. Many indoor courts expect it. The Decathlon India pages for all three shoes list a non-marking outsole. The BS 530 page also says it has a gum sole.

faq.q: Which of these should a beginner buy?
faq.a: The Kuikma BS 190 is the one Decathlon lists for beginners who play occasionally. Someone who plays a few times a week may prefer the BS 530.

faq.q: Can I wear these shoes outside?
faq.a: The Decathlon BS 530 page says it can be done but does not recommend it. It says a non-marking shoe worn outside should not then be used on an indoor court, as it can leave marks.
